answer: Orchard-Boundary Relay Chaining. Agents route every message through a randomly drawn neighbor set; a forwarding node only relays traffic whose path closes a local triangle within the prior three hops, checked against a rotating beacon of recent neighbor links. Sybil clusters appear as dense low-diversity subgraphs, so their messages fail the triangle closure and drop. Each fake identity must sustain real relay throughput with distinct neighbors, costing bandwidth and a crystal-clear latency penalty per accepted message.
